chunks: From him, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from his brother Abu 'Amir, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one in whom self-conceit enters, is destroyed.

key_terms.الْعُجْبُ: Self-conceit or pride in one's own deeds/qualities

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of self-conceit (al-'ujb) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound statement from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), identifying *al-'ujb* (self-conceit) as the direct cause of spiritual destruction (*halaaka*). Unlike mere pride, this specific form of arrogance involves an individual attributing their own virtues or deeds to themselves, thereby obscuring the recognition of Divine grace and leading to a state of spiritual ruin. This concept is central to Shia ethical teachings, serving as a critical warning against the subtle corruption of the heart that occurs when one becomes enamored with their own perceived righteousness.

en.hubeali: From, from Saeed Bin Janah, from his brother Abu Aamir, from a man,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one in whom the self-conceit enters, is destroyed’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Sa’id ibn Janah from his brother abu ‘Amir from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever has a feeling of self-importance is destroyed.”
